explanationMd: Write both bases as powers of three: 3^(2x) = 3^(3x − 3). Equating exponents gives 2x = 3x − 3, so x = 3. Substitution yields 9³ = 27² = 729.

distractorRationale.e: This gives 9 on one side and 1 on the other.
distractorRationale.a: This results from reversing a sign in the exponent equation.
distractorRationale.b: This confuses the ratio of base exponents with the equation’s solution.
